title: Miss Dunlop's gift for the Quothquan Christmas party
source: Hamilton Advertiser, December 29, 1900 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: Ellen Dunlop was providing for village events in Quothquan by 1900.

title: New Year supper and dance in Shieldhill House
source: Hamilton Advertiser, January 4, 1902, page 6 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: Mr and Miss Dunlop, "with their usual generosity," entertained the tenantry, villagers, estate and house servants to a supper and dance in the mansion house. Singers included Messrs Wilson, Henderson and Jackson.

title: Shieldhill Hall, Quothquan (listed building LB12995)
source: Historic Environment Scotland, listed building record LB12995
shows: The corrugated-iron hall in Quothquan was built in 1903 by Nathaniel Dunlop and Miss E. Dunlop for evening services. The listing gives its map position, used for the distance measurements below.

title: Lecture and Christmas party in Shieldhill Hall
source: Hamilton Advertiser, December 30, 1905, page 6 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: A lecture given "through the invitation of Mr and Miss Dunlop," and a Christmas party in Shieldhill Hall, with the Rev. Mr and Mrs Picken present.

title: Quothquan Bowling Club annual social
source: Hamilton Advertiser, March 17, 1906, page 6 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: Nearly every family in the Quothquan district came to the social in the schoolroom; about seventy at supper; a dance followed, with music by Mr and Miss Jackson. No Dunlop is named.

title: Water supply for Mr Dunlop's houses at Quothquan
source: Motherwell Times, May 4, 1906 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: Nathaniel Dunlop applied for a water supply for houses at Quothquan "belonging to him": the Dunlops owned cottages in the village in 1906.

title: Girls' Friendly Society festival at Shieldhill
source: Hamilton Advertiser, July 21, 1906, page 5 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: By Miss Dunlop's invitation, more than seventy members and associates of the Scotch Girls' Friendly Society (a church society for young working women) had a service in the hall, then tea, garden walks and boating at Shieldhill. "Mr Dunlop, on his arrival from the city, gave a cordial welcome to all." No list of names is given.

title: Winter classes and concert in Shieldhill Hall
source: Hamilton Advertiser, April 6, 1907, page 6 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: Classes had run in the hall through the winter, with a governess from Glasgow two days a week and farm servants among the pupils. At the closing concert the laird of Shieldhill was in the chair and Miss Dunlop played; about 200 attended.

title: Nathaniel Dunlop receives an honorary doctorate (LL.D.), Glasgow
source: Glasgow newspapers, April 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: Nathaniel was made an honorary Doctor of Laws on April 23, 1907. Before that he was "Mr" Dunlop, so in the autumn of 1906 the only "Dr Dunlop" in the family was his nephew Binnie.

title: "Dr. Nathaniel Dunlop" at the King's turbine yacht
source: Naval & Military Record, June 6, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: After April 1907 the papers sometimes called Nathaniel "Dr."

title: Shieldhill Estate leases advertised
source: The Scotsman, June 6, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: Estate business at Shieldhill in the month Laurence was born.

title: Nathaniel receives the Thames Conservators in Glasgow
source: The Scotsman, June 22, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: Nathaniel was in Glasgow on June 21, 1907, a week after the birth. No paper places him in Edinburgh between June 14 and July 4.

title: "Dr Nathaniel Dunlop" speaks aboard the Marmion
source: Daily Record, June 22, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: The same Glasgow visit of the Thames Conservators, with Nathaniel styled "Dr."

title: Nathaniel Dunlop named in the King's Birthday Honours as a knight
source: Morning Post, Lloyd's List, Pall Mall Gazette and others, June 28, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: The newspapers reported the birthday honour on June 28, 1907, two weeks after Laurence was born. The investiture at Buckingham Palace followed on July 15.

title: Sir Nathaniel chairs the Clyde Trust in Glasgow
source: Greenock Telegraph and Belfast News-Letter, July 3, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: Nathaniel was in Glasgow on July 2, 1907, two days before Agnes registered the birth in Edinburgh.

title: "Dr. Nathaniel Dunlop," chairman of the Clyde Trust
source: Liverpool Journal of Commerce, October 24, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: Another use of the title "Dr." for Nathaniel after his April 1907 degree.

title: Annual entertainment of the winter evening classes, Quothquan Hall
source: Hamilton Advertiser, April 2, 1910, page 6 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: The classes were still running in 1910. Sir Nathaniel presided; Miss Dunlop was thanked for her interest in the village; "Miss Reid, of Glasgow" sang.

title: Concert in Shieldhill Hall
source: Hamilton Advertiser, April 13, 1912, page 6 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: The hall was still the center of village entertainment in 1912.

title: Women's Rural Institute formed in Shieldhill Hall
source: Hamilton Advertiser, November 16, 1918, page 5 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: Ellen Dunlop's continuing role in the village.

title: Gean Tree Cottage to Shieldhill Hall: about 400 feet
source: Straight-line distance from map coordinates: Historic Environment Scotland position of Shieldhill Hall (55.6404, -3.5975) and Gean Tree Cottage (55.63941, -3.59841)
shows: The home Agnes gave on Laurence's birth entry was about 400 feet from the Dunlops' hall.

title: Royal Maternity Hospital to 18 Lochrin Place: about 0.19 miles
source: Straight-line distance from map coordinates, 79 Lauriston Place to Lochrin Place, Edinburgh
shows: The Douglases, who were raising Laurence by 1911, lived about 330 yards from the hospital where he was born.

title: Registrar's office, 24 Forrest Road: about 0.41 miles from the hospital
source: Straight-line distance from map coordinates; registrar's address from the 1907 Edinburgh directory (see exhibit)
shows: Where Agnes went on July 4, 1907 to register the birth was an easy walk from the hospital.

title: Agnes's Edinburgh homes, 1911–1915: about 1.1 to 1.2 miles from 16 Lochrin Place
source: Straight-line distances from map coordinates: Royal Edinburgh Asylum, Morningside; 9 Stewart Terrace; 62 Balcarres Street; to 16 Lochrin Place
shows: In 1911 Agnes lived and worked in Edinburgh about a mile from 16 Lochrin Place, where her son was being raised as Laurence Douglas. She stayed in Edinburgh after the Douglases moved to Dunfermline in 1912. Gean Tree Cottage is about 25 miles away.

title: Constance Anderson Douglas: "a doctor at the estate" and "a gardener took him in"
source: Laurence's daughter, Constance Anderson Douglas, as told to her son Doug Garceau throughout his life
shows: The records identify a gardener, a physician in the owner’s family and an honorary doctorate for Nathaniel in 1907. The family account names neither candidate and the documents do not identify the father or who first took the baby in.

title: Hamilton Advertiser reports Nathaniel Dunlop's honorary LL.D.
source: Hamilton Advertiser, April 27, 1907, Biggar column (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: The University of Glasgow made Nathaniel Dunlop an honorary Doctor of Laws at its graduation on April 23, 1907, in the presence of the Prince and Princess of Wales.

title: London Gazette: the knighthood at Buckingham Palace
source: The London Gazette, July 26, 1907, issue 28044, page 5118
shows: The King conferred the knighthood on Nathaniel Dunlop of Shieldhill at Buckingham Palace on July 15, 1907. The notice specifies June 28 as the effective date.

title: London Gazette supplement, October 19, 1914
source: The London Gazette, supplement of October 19, 1914, issue 28942, page 8354
shows: Official notice cited in the book's account of the war years.

title: Nathaniel Dunlop: encyclopedia entry
source: Wikipedia: Nathaniel Dunlop
shows: Outline of his life and career with the Allan Line and the Clyde Navigation Trust; checked against the primary records listed here.

title: Royal Maternity Hospital building, 79 Lauriston Place (listed building LB44033)
source: Historic Environment Scotland, listing LB44033
shows: The hospital where Laurence was born still stands; its listing gives the building's history and position, used for the Edinburgh distances.

title: West House, Royal Edinburgh Asylum (listed building LB27718)
source: Historic Environment Scotland, listing LB27718 (Mackinnon House, formerly West House)
shows: The asylum building where Agnes nursed and Thomas McKenzie was an attendant in 1911.

title: Shieldhill House (listed building LB7377)
source: British Listed Buildings / Historic Environment Scotland LB7377
shows: The mansion house of the Shieldhill estate, bought by Nathaniel Dunlop in 1898; now Shieldhill Castle.

title: Ordnance Survey maps of Quothquan and Shieldhill
source: National Library of Scotland, map finder
shows: Period maps showing the house, the village row, the cottages and the hall, used to place Gean Tree and Lime Tree.

title: The Zeppelin raid on Edinburgh and Leith
source: Ian Castle, Zeppelins, Gothas & Giants: 2/3 April 1916
shows: Hour-by-hour account of the raid Laurence lived through at eight.

title: The Zeppelin raid on Edinburgh in 1916
source: The Edinburgh Reporter, October 9, 2022
shows: Where the bombs fell in Edinburgh, with photographs of the damage.

title: The first German air raids on Britain
source: WarHistory.org: The Zeppelin Offensive, 1914–16, Part II
shows: Background to the 1916 raid.

title: North Lawndale, Chicago
source: Encyclopedia of Chicago: North Lawndale
shows: The Chicago neighborhood of 1534 South Kostner Avenue, where Laurence lived with Janet in 1930.

title: The Great New England Hurricane of 1938
source: National Weather Service, Boston
shows: The storm that struck Providence while Laurence was working there.

title: The Hurricane of '38
source: PBS American Experience
shows: The hurricane in Providence.

title: "The '38 Hurricane" by Joe McCarthy
source: American Heritage, August 1969
shows: Eyewitness history of the hurricane.

title: The Great New England Hurricane
source: HISTORY: This Day in History, September 21
shows: Summary of the 1938 hurricane.

title: San Francisco war chronology, 1940–41
source: Museum of the City of San Francisco
shows: San Francisco in the years Laurence worked there and registered for the draft.

title: Historical daily weather records
source: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information: Global Historical Climatology Network – Daily
shows: Historical weather data used for dates in the book.

title: Agnes McGarth, Laurence's great-grandmother, in her later years
source: Family photograph shared on Ancestry by PamelaWills909, December 15, 2018
shows: The wife of William Brown, whose name came down to Laurence's mother.

title: Janet and Laurence with ice-cream cones
source: Family photograph shared on Ancestry by drewgirl (2016) and IZABELLA4213 (2020)
shows: Laurence and Janet Douglas, raised as brother and sister.

title: Laurence Tweedie Brown and Isabella on their fiftieth anniversary
source: Family photograph shared on Ancestry by rwana55
shows: Laurence Tweedie Brown, Agnes's uncle, the "Lawrence" whose name Agnes gave her son.

title: Shieldhill House, now Shieldhill Castle
source: Photograph by Adam Sommerville, geograph.org.uk/photo/1481532, CC BY-SA 2.0
shows: The Dunlops' mansion as it stands today; used as the Evidence Vault background.

title: Gravestone of William Brown and Agnes McGarth
source: Find a Grave memorial 143578503 (photographs by Finches)
shows: Laurence's great-grandparents' grave.

title: Gean Tree Cottage today: estate agent's listing
source: Galbraith, property EDI210051 (sold)
shows: Photographs and a drone video of the cottage Agnes gave as her home in 1907.

title: Gean Tree Cottage: planning approval with drawings
source: South Lanarkshire planning P/26/1249, via City Scope
shows: Current drawings of the cottage.

title: Shieldhill Castle sold to new owners
source: Scottish News, September 14, 2026
shows: Scottish News reported on September 14, 2026 that Mike and Ross Baxter, the founders of House of Gods, had bought Shieldhill Castle. They are a point of contact for an estate-papers inquiry. Whether historical papers passed with the property is unknown.

title: Lloyd's List: the new knight, chairman of the Allan Line and the Clyde Navigation Trust
source: Lloyd's List, June 28, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: Describes Nathaniel Dunlop's two great offices at the moment of his knighthood.

title: "Sir Nathaniel Dunlop of Shieldhill": the local paper's report
source: Hamilton Advertiser, June 29, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: The county paper reports the knighthood of the laird of Shieldhill, fifteen days after Laurence's birth.

title: "A flutter of pleasurable excitement" in Glasgow shipping circles
source: Shipping World and Herald of Commerce, July 3, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: Glasgow's shipping world celebrates his knighthood.

title: "A Distinguished Campbeltonian"
source: Campbeltown Courier, July 6, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: His home town's paper on his knighthood.

title: The Sphere: "Men whom the King honoured on his birthday"
source: The Sphere, July 6, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: A national illustrated paper prints his portrait among the new knights.

title: A record year for the Clyde Trust
source: Belfast News-Letter, July 3, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: As chairman he announces record revenue of £547,758 for the year to June 30, 1907.

title: A new teacher appointed to Quothquan
source: Oban Times, December 29, 1906 and January 12, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: Miss MacLachlan, teacher at Achnacarry, left for an appointment at Quothquan in the winter Agnes was pregnant.

title: Water supply granted to Quothquan schoolhouse
source: Carluke and Lanark Gazette and Hamilton Advertiser, January 26, 1907 (British Newspaper Archive)
shows: County council business in the village that winter.
